tasks.title: Sec A · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What are the speakers mainly talking about?

options.A: How to run one's business successfully.
options.B: How to make progress in one's career.
options.C: Why few people can fully display their capabilities.
options.D: Why young people seldom get the expected promotion.

questions.cn: 两位说话人主要在谈什么？

optionsCn.A: 如何成功地经营自己的生意。
optionsCn.B: 如何在职业上取得进步。
optionsCn.C: 为什么很少有人能充分展示自己的能力。
optionsCn.D: 为什么年轻人很少得到期望中的晋升。

questions.stem: What does the woman say is one mistake people make?

options.A: To mix and interact with peers within the organization.
options.B: To restrict their connections exclusively to colleagues.
options.C: To limit communication only to their superiors.
options.D: To underestimate their role in the company.

questions.cn: 女士说人们常犯的一个错误是什么？

optionsCn.A: 与组织内的同辈交往互动。
optionsCn.B: 把自己的交往对象只限于同事。
optionsCn.C: 把沟通对象只限定在上司身上。
optionsCn.D: 低估自己在公司里的作用。

questions.stem: What does the woman advise people to do in their work?

options.A: Put in quality time.
options.B: Connect with managers.
options.C: Make greater efforts.
options.D: Demonstrate final results.

questions.cn: 女士建议人们在工作中怎么做？

optionsCn.A: 投入有质量的时间。
optionsCn.B: 与管理者建立联系。
optionsCn.C: 付出更大的努力。
optionsCn.D: 展示最终成果。

questions.stem: Why does the man say one should not act like a know-it-all?

options.A: To show their genius.
options.B: To gain due respect.
options.C: To guard against humiliation.
options.D: To avoid appearing arrogant.

questions.cn: 男士为什么说不该表现得无所不知？

optionsCn.A: 为了展示自己的才华。
optionsCn.B: 为了赢得应有的尊重。
optionsCn.C: 为了防止蒙受羞辱。
optionsCn.D: 为了避免显得傲慢。

lines.t: M: Welcome to Business Matters.
lines.cn: M：欢迎收听《商业要务》。

lines.t: M: Today we have invited career development consultant Lucy Williams to talk about how to get ahead at work.
lines.cn: M：今天我们请来了职业发展顾问露西·威廉姆斯，来谈谈如何在职场上获得晋升。

lines.t: M: Hi Lucy.
lines.cn: M：你好，露西。

lines.t: M: Many of us never seem to get promoted.
lines.cn: M：我们很多人似乎永远得不到晋升。

lines.t: M: Why is that and what can we do about it?
lines.cn: M：这是为什么？我们又能做些什么？

lines.t: F: One mistake people make is to limit communication only to their bosses.
lines.cn: F：人们常犯的一个错误，就是把沟通对象只限定在自己的上司身上。

lines.t: F: It's important to expand your network and include your co-workers.
lines.cn: F：扩展你的人脉圈、把同事也纳入进来，这一点很重要。

lines.t: M: But some of our co-workers are less senior to us.
lines.cn: M：可有些同事的职位比我们低。

lines.t: M: Is it really necessary to connect with them?
lines.cn: M：真有必要和他们建立联系吗？

lines.t: F: It's important not to underestimate your colleagues.
lines.cn: F：不要低估你的同事，这一点很重要。

lines.t: F: Sometimes a job title might not clearly demonstrate the influence they may have.
lines.cn: F：有时候，职位头衔并不能清楚体现一个人可能拥有的影响力。

lines.t: M: Now many of us think that working hard creates a good impression, but this isn't always true is it?
lines.cn: M：我们很多人都觉得努力工作能给人留下好印象，但事实并非总是如此，对吧？

lines.t: F: That's right.
lines.cn: F：没错。

lines.t: F: We should avoid trying to take on too much work and constantly staying late just to show that you are committed.
lines.cn: F：我们应当避免为了表现自己很投入，就揽下过多工作、还总是加班到很晚。

lines.t: M: I see.
lines.cn: M：我明白了。

lines.t: M: So setting expectations too high at the beginning can make us look bad if we don't maintain them.
lines.cn: M：所以一开始把期望值定得太高，一旦维持不住，反而会让我们显得很差。

lines.t: F: Yeah, it's better to make sure you are putting in quality time instead of just a large quantity of time.
lines.cn: F：对，与其只拼时间长短，不如确保你投入的是有质量的时间。

lines.t: F: And these efforts can easily be demonstrated by the results we achieve.
lines.cn: F：而且这些付出很容易通过我们取得的成果体现出来。

lines.t: M: What about helping others at work?
lines.cn: M：那在工作中帮助别人呢？

lines.t: M: Should you try and go beyond your normal responsibilities and offer to help people with their projects?
lines.cn: M：是否应该试着超出自己的本职工作范围，主动提出帮别人做项目？

lines.t: F: Extend your assistance to those who need it, but only as long as your own work will not go unattended.
lines.cn: F：可以把帮助给到需要的人，但前提是别耽误了你自己的分内工作。

lines.t: F: If someone can benefit from your assistance or advice, help them out to gain their respect and trust.
lines.cn: F：如果有人能从你的帮助或建议中受益，那就帮他们一把，以此赢得他们的尊重和信任。

lines.t: M: But it goes without saying that you shouldn't act like a know-it-all, otherwise you'll appear arrogant.
lines.cn: M：不过不用说也知道，你不该表现得无所不知，否则会显得傲慢。

lines.t: F: Absolutely.
lines.cn: F：完全正确。

lines.t: F: Be humble and you'll get a lot of time later on to show your genius.
lines.cn: F：保持谦逊，日后你会有大把时间展示自己的才华。

tasks.title: Sec A · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the woman say they first need to do?

options.A: Decide how to divide up the presentation tasks.
options.B: Investigate the available background research.
options.C: Complete the project design together.
options.D: Find a suitable topic for their article.

questions.cn: 女士说他们首先需要做什么？

optionsCn.A: 定下如何划分汇报任务。
optionsCn.B: 调查现有的背景研究。
optionsCn.C: 一起完成项目设计。
optionsCn.D: 为他们的文章找一个合适的题目。

questions.stem: Why does the man refuse to handle the background part?

options.A: He wants to devote his time to other portions.
options.B: He believes the woman is better able to handle it.
options.C: He claims to have done most of the work already.
options.D: He finds the woman more meticulous about details.

questions.cn: 男士为什么拒绝负责背景部分？

optionsCn.A: 他想把时间投入到其他部分。
optionsCn.B: 他认为女士更有能力处理这部分。
optionsCn.C: 他声称自己已经做了大部分工作。
optionsCn.D: 他觉得女士在细节上更一丝不苟。

questions.stem: What does the woman urge the man to stop doing?

options.A: Questioning.
options.B: Complaining.
options.C: Arguing.
options.D: Worrying.

questions.cn: 女士催促男士别再做什么？

optionsCn.A: 质疑。
optionsCn.B: 抱怨。
optionsCn.C: 争辩。
optionsCn.D: 担忧。

questions.stem: Why does the man suggest he present the conclusion and the woman do the introduction?

options.A: To avoid sounding monotonous to the listeners.
options.B: To make the division of labor more reasonable.
options.C: To keep himself from being overburdened.
options.D: To bring their capabilities fully into play.

questions.cn: 男士为什么建议由他讲结论、女士讲引言？

optionsCn.A: 避免让听众觉得单调。
optionsCn.B: 让分工更合理。
optionsCn.C: 使自己不至于负担过重。
optionsCn.D: 让两人的能力充分发挥。

lines.t: F: I think we first need to decide how to divide up the presentation responsibilities.
lines.cn: F：我觉得我们得先定下怎么分派这次汇报的任务。

lines.t: F: From what I recall, the presentation consists of five parts, not including the introduction and conclusion.
lines.cn: F：我记得这个汇报由五个部分组成，不算引言和结论。

lines.t: F: That would mean altogether we need to allocate seven parts between the two of us.
lines.cn: F：也就是说，我们俩一共要分七个部分。

lines.t: F: So we have the abstract, background research, the project design, the results and the discussion portions.
lines.cn: F：那么就是摘要、背景研究、项目设计、结果和讨论这几部分。

lines.t: F: As the abstract section only applies to the article, we needn't include it in the presentation.
lines.cn: F：由于摘要部分只适用于文章本身，我们不必把它放进汇报里。

lines.t: F: How would you suggest we dole out the rest?
lines.cn: F：剩下的你打算怎么分？

lines.t: F: How do you feel about handling the background bit?
lines.cn: F：你来负责背景那部分怎么样？

lines.t: F: In this way, we can both discuss the part of the project that we devoted most of our time to.
lines.cn: F：这样我们都能讲讲自己投入时间最多的那部分。

lines.t: M: Hold on a minute.
lines.cn: M：等一下。

lines.t: M: You want me, the one who did the bulk of the task, to also do the majority of the presentation?
lines.cn: M：你是想让干了大部分活儿的那个人——也就是我——再去承担汇报的大部分？

lines.t: M: The background research which was so meticulous took more than a month.
lines.cn: M：那份做得一丝不苟的背景研究，花了一个多月。

lines.t: F: Okay, okay, I get it.
lines.cn: F：好，好，我明白了。

lines.t: F: Quit your moaning.
lines.cn: F：别抱怨了。

lines.t: F: I appreciate the rigorous work ethic you applied to the research, but not the sarcasm that comes up every time I mention it.
lines.cn: F：我很欣赏你在研究上那份严谨的工作态度，但不喜欢每次我一提这事你就挖苦人。

lines.t: F: What do you think would be a fair arrangement?
lines.cn: F：你觉得怎么分才算公平？

lines.t: M: I think the best arrangement would be to split the research into two parts, before 1980 and afterward.
lines.cn: M：我觉得最好的办法是把研究分成两部分：1980 年以前和以后。

lines.t: M: I will take the before portion and you would be assigned the after 1980, leaving the project and results.
lines.cn: M：我负责前面那段，1980 年之后的归你，项目部分和结果部分另算。

lines.t: M: I volunteer to describe the project, but as I struggled a bit with the statistics in the results section, how about you handling that?
lines.cn: M：我自愿讲项目部分，不过结果部分的统计我有点吃力，那部分你来怎么样？

lines.t: F: That's agreeable to me.
lines.cn: F：我没意见。

lines.t: M: I propose we both handle the discussion section in parts along with the question and answer afterward, leaving only the introduction and conclusion.
lines.cn: M：我建议讨论部分我们俩也分着讲，之后一起应对问答环节，这样只剩下引言和结论了。

lines.t: M: I will take responsibility for the conclusion and put you in charge of the introduction.
lines.cn: M：结论由我负责，引言交给你。

lines.t: M: This will make it so that we alternate presenting, so as to avoid sounding monotonous to the audience.
lines.cn: M：这样我们就能交替上场汇报，避免让听众觉得单调。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What can makeup do, according to new research from the University of Stirling?

options.A: Alter others' perceptions of the wearer.
options.B: Win others' admiration for the wearer.
options.C: Enhance the wearer's confidence.
options.D: Change the wearer's appearance.

questions.cn: 根据斯特灵大学的新研究，化妆能起到什么作用？

optionsCn.A: 改变别人对使用者的看法。
optionsCn.B: 为使用者赢得他人的赞赏。
optionsCn.C: 增强使用者的自信。
optionsCn.D: 改变使用者的外貌。

questions.stem: How did both men and women rate the faces with cosmetics in the new research?

options.A: As being a greater threat.
options.B: As being of higher prestige.
options.C: As being more dominant.
options.D: As being more attractive.

questions.cn: 在这项新研究中，男性和女性如何评价化了妆的面孔？

optionsCn.A: 认为更具威胁。
optionsCn.B: 认为更有声望。
optionsCn.C: 认为更强势。
optionsCn.D: 认为更有吸引力。

questions.stem: Why does a female candidate need to know the gender of the hiring committee members?

options.A: It might influence her way of introducing herself.
options.B: It might impact her dressing style for the occasion.
options.C: It might affect her decision on applying cosmetics.
options.D: It might sway her view on the interviewers' questions.

questions.cn: 女性求职者为什么需要知道招聘委员会成员的性别？

optionsCn.A: 这可能影响她自我介绍的方式。
optionsCn.B: 这可能影响她当天的穿着风格。
optionsCn.C: 这可能影响她是否化妆的决定。
optionsCn.D: 这可能动摇她对面试官提问的看法。

lines.t: Makeup can do more than just change your appearance.
lines.cn: 化妆不只能改变你的外貌。

lines.t: It can also alter others' perceptions of you, for better or for worse.
lines.cn: 它还能改变别人对你的看法——或好或坏。

lines.t: According to new research from the University of Stirling in Scotland, although both men and women perceive women who wear makeup as being of a higher status, men associate makeup with prestigious, positive qualities, while women view other women wearing makeup as being dominant and a potential threat.
lines.cn: 根据苏格兰斯特灵大学的一项新研究，尽管男性和女性都认为化妆的女性地位更高，但男性把化妆与有声望、正面的品质联系在一起，而女性则把化了妆的同性视为强势者和潜在威胁。

lines.t: The research showed that men and women both rated the faces with cosmetics as being more attractive.
lines.cn: 研究显示，男性和女性都认为化了妆的面孔更具吸引力。

lines.t: But only women rated made-up faces as being more dominant, while only men rated made-up faces as being higher in prestige.
lines.cn: 但只有女性认为化了妆的面孔更强势，也只有男性认为化了妆的面孔更有声望。

lines.t: A follow-up study investigated the root cause behind these differences in perception, and found that female on female jealousy seemed to be the main cause for the differences in perception.
lines.cn: 一项后续研究探究了这种认知差异背后的根本原因，发现女性对女性的嫉妒似乎是造成认知差异的主要原因。

lines.t: Women rating women with makeup said they would be more jealous of them, and thought they would be more attractive to men than their non-makeup wearing counterparts.
lines.cn: 评价化妆女性的女性表示，自己会对她们更嫉妒，并认为她们比不化妆的女性更受男性青睐。

lines.t: Cosmetic products are good for more than just giving you a pretty face.
lines.cn: 化妆品的作用不只是让你有一张漂亮的脸。

lines.t: It can be particularly useful for women to understand how wearing makeup alters others' perceptions of them in situations where they are trying to gain others' trust and admiration.
lines.cn: 在人们想要赢得他人信任和赞赏的场合，了解化妆如何改变别人对自己的看法，对女性尤其有用。

lines.t: At a job interview, knowing whether the hiring committee will consist of men or women might influence a female candidate's decision about wearing makeup.
lines.cn: 在求职面试中，知道招聘委员会由男性还是女性组成，可能会影响女性求职者是否化妆的决定。

lines.t: Whether the interviewers will view her as attractive, dominant and prestigious can affect the interviewer's actions and perhaps the outcome of the interview itself.
lines.cn: 面试官会把她看作有吸引力、强势还是有声望，会影响面试官的举动，也许还会影响面试结果本身。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What methods do some advertisements trumpet about changing a habit?

options.A: Those involving no self-recognition.
options.B: Those forcing us to clench our teeth.
options.C: Those resisting various temptations.
options.D: Those requiring no willpower at all.

questions.cn: 一些广告宣扬的是什么样的改变习惯的方法？

optionsCn.A: 那些不涉及自我认知的方法。
optionsCn.B: 那些迫使我们咬紧牙关的方法。
optionsCn.C: 那些抵制各种诱惑的方法。
optionsCn.D: 那些完全不需要意志力的方法。

questions.stem: What does the speaker define willpower as?

options.A: Regulating one's actions for the sake of good health.
options.B: Controlling one's actions with a motivating thought.
options.C: Using practical examples to guide one's behavior.
options.D: Denying oneself any comfort to prevent diseases.

questions.cn: 讲话者把意志力定义为什么？

optionsCn.A: 为了身体健康而规范自己的行为。
optionsCn.B: 用一个激励性的念头控制自己的行为。
optionsCn.C: 用实际例子引导自己的行为。
optionsCn.D: 为预防疾病而拒绝一切安逸。

questions.stem: What may sound amazing enough as regards willpower?

options.A: It equips us with an expert skill.
options.B: It exerts an enduring force on us.
options.C: It leads to a burning goal.
options.D: It begins with a bright idea.

questions.cn: 就意志力而言，什么听起来相当令人称奇？

optionsCn.A: 它赋予我们一项专家技能。
optionsCn.B: 它对我们施加持久的作用力。
optionsCn.C: 它引向一个炽热的目标。
optionsCn.D: 它始于一个妙想。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say may make for effective willpower?

options.A: Any cherished goal.
options.B: Any positive mindset.
options.C: Any personal instinct.
options.D: Any valued role model.

questions.cn: 讲话者说什么能造就有效的意志力？

optionsCn.A: 任何珍视的目标。
optionsCn.B: 任何积极的心态。
optionsCn.C: 任何个人的本能。
optionsCn.D: 任何受重视的榜样。

lines.t: You may have seen advertisements trumpeting methods of changing a habit that require absolutely no willpower whatsoever.
lines.cn: 你可能见过一些广告大肆宣扬改变习惯的方法，说它们完全不需要任何意志力。

lines.t: But can you really change a bad habit or create a good one without willpower?
lines.cn: 但你真的能在没有意志力的情况下改掉坏习惯、养成好习惯吗？

lines.t: To answer this question we first have to ask, what is willpower?
lines.cn: 要回答这个问题，我们得先问：什么是意志力？

lines.t: Most people sadly think of it only as the ability to clench their teeth and resist attractive temptations.
lines.cn: 遗憾的是，多数人只把它看作咬紧牙关、抵制诱人诱惑的能力。

lines.t: In this view, willpower means self-denial and no fun.
lines.cn: 在这种观点里，意志力意味着自我克制、毫无乐趣。

lines.t: No wonder people hope to make changes without it.
lines.cn: 难怪人们希望不靠它就能做出改变。

lines.t: I define willpower as using only the thought of your motivators to control your actions.
lines.cn: 我把意志力定义为：仅凭对自身动力的思考来控制自己的行为。

lines.t: Let's say your motivators are prevent diabetes and reach a healthy weight.
lines.cn: 假设你的动力是预防糖尿病、达到健康体重。

lines.t: So if you are at the all-you-can-eat buffet, you think about your motivator, avoid diabetes through weight loss, and you take small portions and avoid the dessert table.
lines.cn: 那么当你站在自助餐台前时，想一想自己的动力——通过减重来避免糖尿病——于是你只取少量食物，并绕开甜点台。

lines.t: So amazingly enough, willpower begins with a thought, a bright idea, some way to improve your life or contribute to others.
lines.cn: 所以令人惊讶的是，意志力始于一个念头、一个妙想，某种能改善你生活或有助于他人的办法。

lines.t: This bright idea is your motivator.
lines.cn: 这个妙想就是你的动力。

lines.t: Dr. Walter Mischel, an expert on willpower skills, uses the expressive term, a burning goal.
lines.cn: 意志力技能专家沃尔特·米歇尔博士用了一个很传神的说法：一个炽热的目标。

lines.t: Whether you call it a motivator, a burning goal, or a bright idea, this idea is the force behind your willpower.
lines.cn: 无论你称之为动力、炽热的目标，还是妙想，这个想法都是你意志力背后的驱动力。

lines.t: What sort of bright ideas motivators make for effective willpower?
lines.cn: 什么样的妙想（动力）能造就有效的意志力？

lines.t: In fact, any goal that you value strongly counts.
lines.cn: 事实上，任何你极为看重的目标都算。

lines.t: The list may include good health, self-respect, a better future for your family, personal mission, and being a role model for your child.
lines.cn: 这份清单可能包括身体健康、自尊、家人更美好的未来、个人使命，以及成为孩子的榜样。

lines.t: All these can certainly drive a positive change.
lines.cn: 这些当然都能推动积极的改变。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about the federal government's advice on seafood safety?

options.A: It has long been criticized as unclear.
options.B: It has long been ignored by the public.
options.C: It has caused much panic among women.
options.D: It has resulted in different understandings.

questions.cn: 关于联邦政府就海鲜安全提出的建议，讲话者说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它长期以来被批评为不明确。
optionsCn.B: 它长期以来被公众忽视。
optionsCn.C: 它在女性中引起了很大恐慌。
optionsCn.D: 它导致了不同的理解。

questions.stem: What did the Food and Drug Administration do this week?

options.A: It warned consumers not to eat fish from the Gulf of Mexico.
options.B: It called on expectant mothers to pay attention to food safety.
options.C: It issued an update to the advice on seafood consumption.
options.D: It listed more than sixty species of fish as “choices to avoid”.

questions.cn: 美国食品药品监督管理局本周做了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它警告消费者不要吃墨西哥湾的鱼。
optionsCn.B: 它呼吁准妈妈关注食品安全。
optionsCn.C: 它发布了海鲜食用建议的更新版。
optionsCn.D: 它把 60 多种鱼列为“应避免的选择”。

questions.stem: According to the speaker, what are people concerned about regarding pregnant women and seafood?

options.A: The impact of the FDA's analysis.
options.B: Multiple factors including mercury.
options.C: Critics' conclusions.
options.D: The prices of seafood.

questions.cn: 根据讲话者，在孕妇和海鲜问题上人们担心什么？

optionsCn.A: FDA 分析带来的影响。
optionsCn.B: 包括汞在内的多重因素。
optionsCn.C: 批评者的结论。
optionsCn.D: 海鲜的价格。

lines.t: For many pregnant women, understanding what seafood is safe and healthy and what should be avoided because of mercury concerns comes with a lot of worrying.
lines.cn: 对许多孕妇来说，弄清楚哪些海鲜安全健康、哪些因汞的问题应当避免，伴随着一大堆担忧。

lines.t: In part, that's because the federal government's advice on the matter, first issued in 2004, has long been criticized as vague.
lines.cn: 部分原因在于，联邦政府 2004 年首次发布的有关建议长期以来被批评为含糊不清。

lines.t: That guidance has included advice on how much seafood to eat and which species pregnant and breastfeeding women should avoid over concerns about mercury contamination.
lines.cn: 该指导意见包括建议吃多少海鲜，以及出于汞污染的担忧，孕妇和哺乳期女性应避开哪些种类。

lines.t: But critics say the government advisory has done more harm than good, scaring many pregnant and breastfeeding women away from eating seafood altogether.
lines.cn: 但批评者说，这份政府建议弊大于利，把许多孕妇和哺乳期女性吓得干脆完全不吃海鲜了。

lines.t: The problem is real.
lines.cn: 这个问题确实存在。

lines.t: According to a spokesman for the Food and Drug Administration, or FDA for short, the agency analyzed fish consumption data from more than 1,000 pregnant women in the U.S. and found that 21% of them ate no fish whatsoever in the previous month.
lines.cn: 据美国食品药品监督管理局（简称 FDA）的一位发言人说，该机构分析了美国 1000 多名孕妇的鱼类消费数据，发现其中 21% 的人在上个月完全没吃鱼。

lines.t: And those who did eat fish consumed far less than recommended by the dietary guidelines.
lines.cn: 而那些吃了鱼的人，摄入量也远低于膳食指南的推荐。

lines.t: Some 50% ate less than 2 ounces a week and 75% ate less than 4 ounces.
lines.cn: 约 50% 的人每周吃不到 2 盎司，75% 的人吃不到 4 盎司。

lines.t: This week, the FDA issued an update to the advice, listing more than 60 species in a chart that ranks fish as a best choice, good choice, and choices to avoid.
lines.cn: 本周，FDA 发布了这份建议的更新版，在一张图表中列出 60 多个鱼类品种，并将其划分为“最佳选择”“良好选择”和“应避免的选择”。

lines.t: The goal is to make it easier for mothers to be to feel confident about the type of seafood they include in their diets.
lines.cn: 这样做的目的，是让准妈妈们对自己饮食中摄入的海鲜种类更放心。

lines.t: The new advice recommends consumers choose a variety of fish to eat, and it comes with an easy to understand illustration of what an appropriate portion size should be.
lines.cn: 新建议推荐消费者选择多种鱼类食用，并配有一张通俗易懂的图，说明合适的食用份量。

lines.t: Four ounces for an adult and two ounces for children aged 4 to 7.
lines.cn: 成人为 4 盎司，4 至 7 岁儿童为 2 盎司。

lines.t: And while expectant mothers have long been warned to stay away from shark and four other particular types of fish from the Gulf of Mexico, now there are three new species on the list of what to avoid.
lines.cn: 长期以来，准妈妈们一直被提醒远离鲨鱼以及另外四种来自墨西哥湾的鱼，如今“应避免”清单上又新增了三个品种。

lines.t: But not everyone is thrilled with the new advice.
lines.cn: 但并非所有人都对这份新建议感到满意。

lines.t: Critics say the new advice doesn't always agree with the agency's own scientific findings.
lines.cn: 批评者说，新建议并不总是与该机构自身的科学结论一致。

lines.t: While mercury is of great concern when people are talking about pregnant women and seafood, it's not the only factor contributing to anxiety.
lines.cn: 虽然谈到孕妇和海鲜时，汞是备受关注的问题，但它并非引发焦虑的唯一因素。

lines.t: The FDA maintains that its final consumption recommendations were based on thorough scientific analysis.
lines.cn: FDA 坚持认为，其最终的食用建议基于全面的科学分析。

lines.t: Agency spokesman Kassell says the FDA believes the recommendations will increase confidence, not uncertainty.
lines.cn: 该机构发言人卡塞尔说，FDA 相信这些建议会增强信心，而不是带来不确定性。

lines.t: But critics disagree.
lines.cn: 但批评者并不认同。

lines.t: They think the FDA's advice is not based on the evidence in its own detailed report, and so it confuses everyone.
lines.cn: 他们认为 FDA 的建议并非基于其自身详细报告中的证据，因而让所有人都感到困惑。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about people not taking any vacation?

options.A: They will suffer a breakdown soon.
options.B: They will be losing both joy and life.
options.C: They will be putting themselves and family at risk.
options.D: They will make things worse for people around them.

questions.cn: 关于不休假的人，讲话者说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们很快就会精神崩溃。
optionsCn.B: 他们既会失去快乐，也可能失去生命。
optionsCn.C: 他们会使自己和家人陷入危险。
optionsCn.D: 他们会把身边人的处境弄得更糟。

questions.stem: What does the nine-year study recommend people do when planning vacations?

options.A: Spend 14 days for vacation every year.
options.B: Aim for three separate vacations yearly.
options.C: Space out their vacations evenly instead of taking one long vacation.
options.D: Use all their days off for a long summer break to achieve full-on calm.

questions.cn: 那项为期九年的研究建议人们在安排假期时怎么做？

optionsCn.A: 每年休假 14 天。
optionsCn.B: 争取一年休三次假。
optionsCn.C: 把假期均匀间隔开，而不是一次休一个长假。
optionsCn.D: 把所有休息日用来放一个长暑假，以达到完全的平静。

questions.stem: Why is vacation frequency important, according to the speaker?

options.A: Expecting to have more vacations in a year will boost one's work efficiency.
options.B: Anticipating more vacations would reduce one's feelings of despair at work.
options.C: Taking more than three vacations yearly would prolong one's excitement.
options.D: Planning multiple breaks throughout the year will add to one's happiness.

questions.cn: 根据讲话者，为什么休假频次很重要？

optionsCn.A: 期待一年中有更多假期会提高工作效率。
optionsCn.B: 期待更多假期会减少工作中的沮丧感。
optionsCn.C: 一年休假超过三次会延长兴奋感。
optionsCn.D: 一年中安排多次休息会增加快乐。

lines.t: I know you're busy with work, but you also need to take some time off to recharge those batteries.
lines.cn: 我知道你工作很忙，但你也需要抽点时间休息，好让自己重新充电。

lines.t: So, should you plan one big vacation for the year?
lines.cn: 那么，你是该为这一年安排一次大长假？

lines.t: Or should you take multiple short vacations throughout?
lines.cn: 还是该在一年中安排多次短假？

lines.t: Quantity can sometimes beat quality.
lines.cn: 数量有时能胜过质量。

lines.t: First and foremost, regardless of how you use your vacation days, you need to be using them, and soon.
lines.cn: 首先，无论你怎么用年假，你都得用起来，而且要尽快。

lines.t: The longer you put off your time off, the worse you're making things for yourself.
lines.cn: 休假拖得越久，你给自己造成的处境就越糟。

lines.t: One nine-year-long study published in psychosomatic medicine suggests not taking at least one vacation a year may increase your risk of mortality due to heart disease.
lines.cn: 发表在《心身医学》上的一项长达九年的研究表明，每年连一次假都不休，可能增加因心脏病死亡的风险。

lines.t: So, not only are you killing your joy, you're possibly killing yourself.
lines.cn: 所以，你不只是在毁掉自己的快乐，还可能是在毁掉自己的健康。

lines.t: Give yourself a break, folks.
lines.cn: 给自己放个假吧，各位。

lines.t: When you should take those breaks, however, depends on a few factors.
lines.cn: 不过，什么时候休假取决于几个因素。

lines.t: How many days you have available to use, what activities bring you joy, whether you have a family or not, and other variables come into play.
lines.cn: 你有多少天可用、什么活动能让你快乐、你有没有家庭，以及其他一些变量都会起作用。

lines.t: Because of that, there's no perfect formula that works for everyone, but there are still a few things everyone can try to shoot for.
lines.cn: 正因如此，没有一套适合所有人的完美公式，但仍有几点是每个人都可以努力做到的。

lines.t: We know that, in terms of maximizing relaxation, you should aim for vacations that range somewhere between seven and eleven days long.
lines.cn: 我们知道，就最大程度放松而言，假期的长度应瞄准 7 到 11 天之间。

lines.t: That gives you enough time to let go of your stress at work, completely loosen up, and achieve full-on calm.
lines.cn: 这样你才有足够时间放下工作压力、彻底松弛下来，达到完全的平静。

lines.t: That above-mentioned study also recommends you space out your vacations evenly instead of using up all of your days at once.
lines.cn: 上述那项研究还建议，把假期均匀间隔开，而不是一次把假期用完。

lines.t: Eight days might sound like a lot for someone who only gets ten days of vacation a year, but if you frame them with weekends, you can manage two evenly spaced eight-day vacations a year.
lines.cn: 对一年只有十天假的人来说，八天听起来可能很多，但如果把它们和周末连起来算，你一年可以安排两次间隔均匀的八天假期。

lines.t: If you have fourteen days of paid leave, that's almost three separate eight-day vacations you can use to split your year into thirds.
lines.cn: 如果你有 14 天带薪假，那差不多可以分成三次独立的八天假期，把一年分成三段。

lines.t: As tempting as it might be to use all your days to take one long summer break, your overall goal should be to achieve the perfect balance between length plus joy and frequency.
lines.cn: 尽管把假期一次用来放个长长的暑假很诱人，但你的总体目标应该是在时长、快乐和频次之间取得完美平衡。

lines.t: Vacation frequency is important because planning multiple breaks throughout the year means you always have something to look forward to.
lines.cn: 休假频次之所以重要，是因为一年中安排多次休息意味着你总有值得期待的事。

lines.t: Planning things and the anticipation that comes with it tends to make us happier.
lines.cn: 做计划以及随之而来的期待，往往会让我们更快乐。

lines.t: If you only take one long vacation every year, the excitement builds much more slowly and seems so far off that it can actually lead to feelings of despair.
lines.cn: 如果你每年只休一次长假，兴奋感积累得慢得多，而且看起来那么遥远，实际上可能引发沮丧感。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 3 组
tasks.context: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What are researchers doing in Sweden?

options.A: Surveying when drivers are caught in the heat of arguments.
options.B: Designing devices to prevent drivers from being distracted.
options.C: Testing models for monitoring drivers easily getting tired.
options.D: Developing sensor-based systems for autonomous vehicles.

questions.cn: 研究人员在瑞典做什么？

optionsCn.A: 调查司机何时会卷入激烈争吵。
optionsCn.B: 设计装置以防司机分心。
optionsCn.C: 测试便于监测易疲劳司机的模型。
optionsCn.D: 为自动驾驶汽车开发基于传感器的系统。

questions.stem: What did the researchers' project aim to do, according to Dr. Anna Anund?

options.A: Make sure the autonomous vehicle operates in the simplest manner.
options.B: Ensure the transition from the driver to the vehicle is safely made.
options.C: Alleviate the driver's pressure as much as possible.
options.D: Record the driver's state as accurately as possible.

questions.cn: 根据安娜·阿努德博士，这个研究项目的目标是什么？

optionsCn.A: 确保自动驾驶汽车以最简单的方式运行。
optionsCn.B: 确保从司机到车辆的交接安全完成。
optionsCn.C: 尽可能缓解司机的压力。
optionsCn.D: 尽可能准确地记录司机的状态。

questions.stem: What is thought to be responsible for a fifth of road accidents across the European Union?

options.A: Driver fatigue.
options.B: Dreadful traffic.
options.C: Drunk driving.
options.D: Driving time.

questions.cn: 在整个欧盟，什么被认为是五分之一道路事故的原因？

optionsCn.A: 司机疲劳。
optionsCn.B: 糟糕的交通状况。
optionsCn.C: 酒后驾车。
optionsCn.D: 驾驶时长。

questions.stem: Why do drivers now view self-driving cars as less safe than they used to?

options.A: There has been a strong debate on the feasibility of Level 3 cars.
options.B: There have been few remarkable advances in auto technology.
options.C: There has been a rise in attention-grabbing accidents recently.
options.D: There have been few feasible ways to shift public sentiment.

questions.cn: 为什么司机们现在认为自动驾驶汽车不如过去安全？

optionsCn.A: 关于第 3 级汽车可行性的激烈讨论一直存在。
optionsCn.B: 汽车技术几乎没有显著的进步。
optionsCn.C: 近来引人注目的事故有所增加。
optionsCn.D: 几乎没有可行的办法来改变公众情绪。

lines.t: Autonomous cars that can take over from drivers if they are tired or distracted are being developed in Sweden.
lines.cn: 瑞典正在研发能在司机疲劳或分心时接管驾驶的自动驾驶汽车。

lines.t: Researchers working as part of the European Union's 77 billion euro research program are developing sensor-based systems that monitor whether a driver is distracted, anxious, or tired.
lines.cn: 参与欧盟 770 亿欧元研究项目的研究人员正在开发基于传感器的系统，用来监测司机是否分心、焦虑或疲劳。

lines.t: If a driver is not in a fit state to be on the road, the car automatically takes control of the wheel to prevent accidents.
lines.cn: 如果司机状态不适合上路，汽车会自动接管方向盘，以防止事故发生。

lines.t: Dr. Anna Anund from the Swedish National Road and Transport Research Institute, who is leading the project, said a driver's state can be measured using a number of sensors, including heart rate monitors and eye sensors, which track where a driver's gaze is.
lines.cn: 该项目负责人、瑞典国家道路与运输研究所的安娜·阿努德博士说，可以用多种传感器来测量司机的状态，包括心率监测器和追踪司机视线方向的眼睛传感器。

lines.t: She said the aim was to really make sure that the transition from the driver to the vehicle is done in a safe way, so we can take into consideration the driver's state, and so we do not give control to a driver who is under pressure of fatigue, stress, anxiety, and so on.
lines.cn: 她说，目标是要真正确保从司机到车辆的交接以安全方式进行，这样我们就能把司机的状态考虑进去，不会把控制权交给处于疲劳、压力、焦虑等状态下的司机。

lines.t: According to data from the European Commission, Sweden has the safest roads in the EU, with the UK a close second.
lines.cn: 根据欧盟委员会的数据，瑞典拥有欧盟最安全的道路，英国紧随其后。

lines.t: However, the number of road accidents in both has largely leveled out since 2010.
lines.cn: 然而自 2010 年以来，两国道路事故的数量大体上已趋于平稳。

lines.t: Driver fatigue is thought to be responsible for as many as a fifth of road crashes across the EU, although there are certain times of the day when more accidents happen.
lines.cn: 在整个欧盟，多达五分之一的车祸被认为与司机疲劳有关，不过一天中某些时段事故更易发生。

lines.t: At 6am, for example, drivers are said to be 20 times more likely to have an accident than at 10am.
lines.cn: 例如，清晨 6 点发生事故的可能性据说是上午 10 点的 20 倍。

lines.t: While most experts agree driverless technology should help bring down accident numbers in the long term, some have questioned whether it is safe.
lines.cn: 尽管多数专家认同无人驾驶技术从长远看应有助于降低事故数量，但有些人质疑它是否安全。

lines.t: The researchers have said the technology they are developing is seeking to bridge the gap between level 3 on the autonomy scale, in which drivers have to be ready to take control of the car at any point, and level 4, in which driving is automated.
lines.cn: 研究人员表示，他们正在开发的技术旨在弥合自动驾驶分级中第 3 级（司机须随时准备接管汽车）与第 4 级（驾驶完全自动化）之间的空白。

lines.t: Daniel Ruiz, the chief executive of the UK's Connected and Autonomous Vehicle Program, Meridian, said, There is a strong debate going on about how it is possible to make a level 3 car completely safe.
lines.cn: 英国互联与自动驾驶汽车项目 Meridian 的首席执行官丹尼尔·鲁伊斯说：“关于如何让第 3 级汽车做到完全安全，目前正有一场激烈的讨论。”

lines.t: Despite advances in technology, we still have some way to go in shifting public sentiment.
lines.cn: 尽管技术不断进步，我们在改变公众情绪方面仍有很长的路要走。

lines.t: With an increase in attention grabbing accidents recently, drivers now view self-driving cars as less safe than they used to.
lines.cn: 随着近来引人注目的事故增多，司机们现在认为自动驾驶汽车不如过去安全了。
